correctness.rationale: The union of x↦(x,±x²) over F_p intersects only at (0,0), hence the convolution kernel is the sum of two quadratic exponential sums minus 1. For v=0 it contributes 3p-2 to the total absolute kernel sum. For u=0, the quadratic Gauss sums contribute B_p; for u,v!=0 the change t=u²/(4v) gives each t exactly p-1 times, with kernel 2sqrt(p)chi(t)cos(2pi t/p)-1 for p=1 mod4 or the analogous sine for p=3 mod4. The l-infinity convolution norm is p^-2 times the l1 kernel. Riemann sums for |sin|/|cos| give 2p/pi and the signed Legendre-character term has O(sqrt(p)log p) interval cancellation; both branches yield (4/pi)sqrt(p)+O(log p/sqrt(p)). Unit-normalization checks give single-parabola (1+(p-1)sqrt(p))/p and Fourier ratio (2sqrt2/pi)p+O(log p). No composite moduli or arbitrary weights are claimed.
residual_risks: Finite experiments do not prove unrestricted statements; proof deductions above carry general assertion.
